rename.from: Template param not being applied correctly
rename.to: Method return type not being inferred for templated class

body:
Psalm does not infer closure type from context, and it needs its type to infer the resulting type of `map()`.
https://psalm.dev/r/b6908489aa is the way to make it pass.
Yeah, it only checks the boundaries (so it’d complain if the param was `Optional<int>`). There’s some special handling, IIRC, for `array_map`, but that’s about it.
That's a shame. Is that a technical limitation or a design choice? I'd rather not have to write type declarations & doc blocks which can be inferred. Especially once arrow functions land.
@muglug I'm not sure if GitHub notifies for comments in closed issues, so ... ^
Psalm's behaviour is also different from HHVM's - I've opened a ticket at https://github.com/facebook/hhvm/issues/8496 because maybe I'm just wrong.

> The two cases are treated differently by TypeScript and Java I believe

Can you provide examples?
Yeah, you've convinced me that this is something Psalm should do.
I'm going to solve it for when param types aren't given, not sure about return types.

And it'll be even better [in PHP 7.4](https://wiki.php.net/rfc/arrow_functions_v2) - 

```php
return $collection->map(function ($o) { return $o->get(); });
```

will become

```php
return $collection->map(fn($o) => $o->get());
```
That works with single-closure expression only, right? `$collection->map($f = function($o) { return $o->get(); });` is out of scope?
